topic.title: Where Your Money Goes When You Swipe
topic.hook: The invisible chain taking a cut
topic.payoff: The invisible chain taking a cut

copy.title: FOLLOW THE MONEY WHEN YOU SWIPE

steps.rule: Trace the swipe before you spend
steps.why: every card transaction routes through at least three separate businesses before settling, each extracting a slice.

steps.rule: Count every hand in the chain
steps.why: the processor, the network, and the issuing bank each hold a toll gate the merchant has already priced into your total.

steps.rule: Multiply one purchase across a year
steps.why: forty dollars a week is two thousand and eighty a year, and the chain collects its percentage on every single dollar.

steps.rule: Spot who designed the friction away
steps.why: contactless payment removed the pause that once made spending feel real, and volume rose the moment hesitation did not.

steps.rule: Name whose model your habit funds
steps.why: reward points are not free money, they are the chain recycling a fraction of what it already collected from the merchant on your behalf.

copy.kicker: The swipe is fast. The chain is long.
copy.thumb_scene: Wick stands upright on a plain white studio background, one arm extended holding a single payment card out flat like an exhibit, his other hand pointing down a long paper receipt that coils to the floor beside him, his expression flat and deliberate, nothing else in frame.
copy.send_to: the friend who earns cashback and calls it winning

caption:
Most people think the reward points are the whole game.

They aren't.

The chain was paid before you ever got to the checkout screen.

The hidden rule is this: every frictionless payment system is an architecture built to increase volume, and the less you feel a purchase, the more the chain earns across the year.

Forty dollars a week is two thousand and eighty dollars a year. The percentage rides on every dollar, every time.

Watch your next tap.

When did you first notice the pause was gone? Drop it below.
